title: Keel Town Quarterly
summary: The Keel Town mail only goes up by winch and by courier, and the winch is cheaper, so guess whose job this is. Quarterly bag — letters, two cargo manifests someone wrote poems in the margins of, and one taped parcel marked 'DO NOT READ ALOUD'. Up the mesa, then back down the long way: Devanna wants your landings getting worse on record, not by accident.

objectives.label: Take the Keel Town mail bag from the job board
Take the winch ramp up the mesa
Deliver the mail bag in Keel Town
Collect the return pouch from the dockmaster's hut
Run the pouch home — landings to practice

offer.text: Quarterly mail for Keel Town. Normally the winch does it, but the winch has filed a complaint — about *gravity*, courier, I cannot make this stuff up — and so the bag moves by Driftline at double rate.
One condition from the dockmaster: come down the long way, around the north shoulder. She says your landings are 'promising', which from Devanna Shore is a declaration of love.
A bag that could ride a cable, a dockmaster grading my landings, and the Guild paying double so a machine can sulk. This job is perfect.

accept.text: The parcel marked DO NOT READ ALOUD — do not. The last courier who did read one aloud was fine, but the meeting he read it *to* required a recess. Mind the winch cables near the base; they hum when the ships above are arguing.

Ketch here. Climb the ramp steady, no boost near the lip — the updraft off the mesa face will take a hot engine and be rude with it. Coming down, feather it. Wisp will be watching. Everyone's always watching up there, kid. It's a *dock*.
Friend Varga, traffic report: you, shortly. The mesa is looking forward to it. Upstairs is clear, downstairs is patient, the winch is in a *mood*. Come up the friendly side.

complete.text: Mail received, pouch countersigned. Watched your descent, courier. Not bad. That is the whole compliment; do not spend it all at once.
Bag up, pouch down, double rate earned, and the Guild's ledger records the winch's complaint as 'resolved by subcontract'. The machine gets an apology. You get credits. The system works.
Traffic clears, friend. For the record: your last landing was a nine. I'm rounding, but I'm *kind*.
